name: Beef Chili Rice Bowls
intro_html: A big pot of hearty beef chili, spooned over rice and topped with melty cheddar. This is cold-weather comfort that meal-preps like a champion, gets better on day two, and still brings {{protein}} grams of protein a bowl. Make a batch on Sunday and lunch is handled all week.
ingredients_display: 93/7 Ground Beef (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans, drained (910 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 1/2 cups, drained (420 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 3.5 cups dry jasmine: ~$0.86. Buy 1 (covers this batch with some left over).
Seasoned Black Beans, 4 cans, drained: ~$5.94. Buy 4 cans: $6.66.
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 2 1/2 cups, drained: ~$0.80. Buy 1 can: $0.82.
Beef Broth, about 1 3/4 cups: ~$0.64. Buy 1 (covers about two batches).
Fat Free Cheddar, about 1 3/4 cups shredded: ~$1.94. Buy 1 8oz bag: $2.25.
Pantry seasonings (taco seasoning): ~$0.52. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $35.11 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.51 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $39.98 across 14 servings, roughly $2.86 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $1.08 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $41.06. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a filling, protein-packed chili that tastes like it took all day.
shop_smart: Beef on sale, frozen, wins again. This is the ingredient that drives the cost, so buy it low and freeze it.
Tomato paste is pennies and it deepens the whole pot. Freeze leftover paste in tablespoon dollops for next time.
Canned beans and corn by the case shave a little off each can and you will reach for them again next week.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Brown the ground beef with the diced yellow onion in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking the beef up. Drain any excess.
Stir in the tomato paste and taco seasoning and cook for a minute to bloom the flavor.
Add the drained beans, corn, and beef broth. Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until it thickens into a chili.
Serve each bowl over rice and top with the shredded cheddar.
portion_html: Weigh the rice and the chili together, subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1, and divide the total by 14. Scoop equal amounts into each container. Every bowl lands near {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.
